conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for making time for this today. I’m Claire, a perinatal mental-health clinician. Over the next few minutes I’d like to complete the Edinburgh Postpartum/Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS, with you. It’s a short set of ten questions we use with every new mum to see how your mood, thoughts, and energy have been feeling since your baby arrived. Nothing you share leaves this room, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you this past week. We’ll go one question at a own pace; if anything feels hard to talk about, we can pause or re-word it. Ready to start?

First question: Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things—would you say as much as ever, not quite as much, definitely not so much now, or not at all?

Good morning. Yes, let’s go ahead.

I’d say “not quite as much.” I still laugh sometimes—like when my partner makes a joke or the baby does something silly—but it feels a little forced, like I have to remind myself to enjoy it instead of it just happening naturally.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I’ve been able to laugh and see the funny side of things—not quite as much as I used to, though.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I’ve looked forward with enjoyment to things… definitely not so much now. I still plan little outings or visits, but the excitement I used to feel isn’t really there. Mostly I’m just thinking about whether the baby will sleep or if I’ll have the energy to get through it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

I do catch myself doing that sometimes—like if the baby’s fussy and won’t settle, I’ll think maybe I missed his sleepy window or didn’t feed him right. It’s not every time, and I know rationally it’s not my fault, but those “what did I do wrong?” thoughts still pop in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, a bit. I’ll be sitting there feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing, worrying something might be wrong—even when she’s perfectly fine. It’s not constant, but it happens most days, and I can’t always pin it on anything specific.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
I haven’t really had that panicky feeling, just the worries I already mentioned. No sudden sweats or racing heart for no reason—just the ordinary new-mum nerves.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, sometimes. Not every moment, but there are stretches—especially in the late afternoon when the baby’s been clingy and I’m running on a couple hours of broken sleep—where I feel like I’m barely treading water. I’ll look at the dishes or the laundry and think, “I just can’t today,” but I still manage to get through it.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly. I do have trouble falling and staying asleep, but it’s more because I’m listening for every little noise the baby makes or running through the next feed in my head. I wouldn’t say I’m “so unhappy” that it keeps me awake—just wired and a bit on edge.
I have felt sad or miserable

I have felt sad or miserable… yes, sometimes. It’s not there all day, but little waves hit me—like when I’m rocking the baby at 3 a.m. and suddenly feel like crying for no clear reason. Maybe a few times this week, and they pass after a bit.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t cried at all this week. I’ve felt teary a couple of times, but the tears never actually came.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, not at all. I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 10: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: New mother, ≤ 3 mo post-delivery (per clinical context)

Symptoms endorsed (EPDS‐10 key items)  
- Anhedonia & reduced enjoyment (Q1, Q2)  
- Frequent self-blame/guilt when baby fussy (Q3)  
- Unwarranted daily anxiety/worry without clear trigger (Q4)  
- Intermittent “waves” of sadness/misery, 3 a.m. episodes (Q8)  
- Feeling “on top of me,” especially late afternoon with sleep deprivation (Q6)  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance difficulties driven by hyper-vigilance to infant, not low mood per se (Q7)

Symptoms denied  
- Panic attacks (Q5)  
- Actual crying spells (Q9)  
- Self-harm ideation (Q10)

Risk factors / screening significance  
- Sub-syndromal depressive features (anhedonia, intermittent dysphoria)  
- Postpartum anxiety (daily, non-specific)  
- Fatigue and coping depletion, no social supports mentioned  
- No current safety concerns (no suicidal/harm ideation)

Screening impression  
Elevated risk for postpartum depression and anxiety; scores fall in “possible” range (formal scoring recommended). No red-flag safety issues at present. Continue monitoring, consider full EPDS scoring and follow-up within 1–2 weeks or sooner if worsening mood, functioning, or any thoughts of self-harm develop.
